items.text: One implementation answers +new-window, +split, +rename and +list's layout on Windows and Linux.
A relay window open when Ghoztty quits comes back at the next launch.
On Linux a pane's shell now outlives the app: closing it yourself still ends it.
The Linux viewer-pane card is split into eleven ordered slices.
The Linux app links WebKitGTK and its viewer renders markdown, code, local pages and websites.
Linux viewer tests skip their POSIX-only path asserts on Windows, and the test-reach audit knows a pure gtk module runs in every lane.
On Linux, +split --view and +new-window --view open viewer panes in the split tree.
A test sandbox can no longer auto-update the user's installed Ghoztty.
A copy of Ghoztty that is not the installed one no longer runs the installer over the real install.
self-spawn-audit is green again: the GTK app's agent lookup was already guarded.
The update harnesses refuse to install anything that could reach the user's Ghoztty, and prove afterwards it did not move.
Every test that runs the real Windows installer now refuses a package that could reach the user's Ghoztty, and an audit keeps it that way.
